name: What is the difference between multifamily construction and apartment building construction?

mainEntity.name: Are multifamily construction and apartment building construction the same thing, or do they refer to different project types?
mainEntity.text: Are multifamily construction and apartment building construction the same thing, or do they refer to different project types?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multifamily construction is the umbrella term used for any project with more than one residential unit on a single site. That includes apartment buildings, duplexes, triplexes, fourplexes, stacked flats, courtyard buildings, and some mixed-use developments with housing above commercial space. Apartment building construction is narrower and usually refers to larger rental-focused buildings. The distinction matters because the project type can affect design decisions, permitting paths, parking requirements, and financing expectations. A duplex or four-unit building may be reviewed very differently from a larger apartment complex, even if both are called multifamily. That also affects who should be hired, because some contractors are stronger on low-rise residential buildings while others specialize in denser urban apartment work. For owners and developers, using the correct term helps when requesting bids, confirming scope, and comparing proposals. The best pages on this topic should explain the differences in plain language and show which project types are included under each label.
acceptedAnswer.description: Multifamily construction is the broader category and includes apartments, duplexes, triplexes, townhome-style residential buildings, and mixed-use residential projects. Apartment building construction usually refers to larger rental buildings with multiple stacked units. In practice, the terms overlap, but multifamily is the more accurate umbrella term for design, permitting, and construction planning.
